method: Three independent judges (research/phase6/judge_ev.json, judge_ceiling.json, judge_integrity.json) read the full record after two red-team rounds and proposed picks without seeing each other; all three converged. The orchestrator adopted the consensus.
headline: No venture-scale opportunity to make RAM, or something better than RAM, in the U.S. survived for a founder with under $50k. The best available moves are a capped, gated software side business sold to memory buyers, a sequenced fallback, and a ~$0 option on a contract-reference price index.

PRIMARY.label: Memory Lifecycle & Cost Intelligence SaaS for small U.S. hardware OEMs (EOL/PCN alerts, NVM cross-reference, last-time-buy sizer & studies) — run as a gated side business, not a venture
PRIMARY.economics: BASE ARR ~$69.9k at m18 / ~$149.6k at m36 (GLUT $104.1k, SEVERE $83.0k at m36); breakeven m17 with founder unpaid; never pays a $10k/month salary within 36 months unless trial conversion >=14.7% (models/lifecycle-intel.py; 04_DEEPDIVES/lifecycle-intel.md §14)
PRIMARY.gate: K0 written employer carve-out by 2026-11-09 (else stop); K6 25 qualified cold calls booked in 21 days and K1 >=5 of 25 refundable $500 deposits/paid LOIs at >=$200/mo by 2026-12-01; K5 data-terms by 2026-12-15
PRIMARY.spend: <=$500 before K0; ~$1,950 planned for the 29-day test (~$2,950 if the $1,000 government-contracts consult is not deferred — it is deferred until K3+K4 pass); <=$5,000 hard cap; <=$34k ever; $5k cash floor
PRIMARY.plan_cash: Plan-accurate cash (models/lifecycle-intel.py section 10 PLAN rows, re-run 2026-11-01, exit 0; BASE itself charges no test spend and books the $5k antitrust opinion at m2). PLAN = the $1,950 test charged at m1, the $5k antitrust opinion and $1k consult deferred: max founder draw $30,850 (within the <=$34k cap), cash low $9,150 at m16 (above the $5k floor); GLUT $9,784, SEVERE $10,112. PLAN + index option passes (K3+K4 pass; $2,950 at m1 and the $5k opinion at m2): max draw $36,850 and cash low $3,150 at m16, i.e. over the cap and under the floor unless results beat BASE; the cap and floor still bind. PLAN with K5 failed (price line deleted): cash low $3,997 at m22, below the floor.
PRIMARY.embedded_tests: C-72 (legacy-DRAM buying co-op) is killed as a standalone concept under Rule 1 at the Phase 7 gate; its three supplier calls ride along inside DD2's kill test at $0.
PRIMARY.post_pass_gates: Per 04_DEEPDIVES/lifecycle-intel.md §11: >=2 paying accounts by 2027-08-31 (m9) else stop; by 2027-11-30 (m12) >=5 paying accounts AND MRR >=$1,700 — missing either stops the build (code to maintenance); stop if cash falls below $5k; by m18 >=13 accounts or open exit talks (Lytica, Z2Data, Accuris, Supplyframe, Luminovo).

FALLBACK.label: OpenRAM macro service for U.S. open-PDK tapeouts (sky130/GF180) — wedge only; sequenced, never parallel to DD2
FALLBACK.economics: BASE ARR ~$41.2k at m18 / ~$65.7k at m36 (GLUT $54.9k, SEVERE $49.3k); breakeven m12 founder unpaid; never pays a salary (models/open-memory-ip.py; 04_DEEPDIVES/open-memory-ip.md §14)
FALLBACK.gate: $0 written no-release statements from UCSC VLSIDA and Open Circuit Design first (silence = fail); then >=2 buyers at >=$10k; then contractor-signed 16 KB corner + Monte Carlo; >=3 paid deposits or >=$15k LOIs
FALLBACK.spend: $0 in Nov 2026 (letters only); <=$9.1k only if DD2 fails on 2026-12-01 and both no-release statements arrive
FALLBACK.timing_note: DD5's model and §10 dates assume a November 2026 start; as FALLBACK it runs only after DD2 fails on 2026-12-01, so its paid steps shift ~2 months (Jan-Feb 2027) — see FIRST_90_DAYS.md branch B. Its $0 written questions (test iv) still go out in week 1.

MOONSHOT.label: NONE honestly qualifies. Best available: a contract-reference Memory Cost Escalation Index (C-86, killed as designed by the red team) held as a ~$0-marginal option inside DD2's kill test
MOONSHOT.economics: Only credible >$2M path in the study (03_SCORING.md §6: $2-10M ARR upside if it becomes the reference index cited in contracts); ceiling judge puts odds at ~3%
MOONSHOT.gate: K3 >=2 signed LOIs naming a live contract/surcharge schedule that would cite the index (and why TrendForce/open-book doesn't serve it) + K4 >=10 signed PO-price contribution agreements, inside the DD2 test window
MOONSHOT.spend: $0 marginal (asks ride on DD2 calls); defer the $1k gov-contracts and $5k antitrust opinions until K3+K4 pass
MOONSHOT.confidence: All three judges agree no MOONSHOT honestly qualifies (judge confidence in that call: 0.7-0.8; the ceiling judge's 0.03 is the odds that the C-86 option itself succeeds)
MOONSHOT.funding_rule: Funding rule (Phase 7): if K3+K4 pass, the deferred $6k of index legal work (the $5k antitrust opinion + $1k gov-contracts consult) is spent only if it is covered by (a) index pre-sale deposits/LOI prepayments of >=$6k or (b) a <=$10k convertible note from an index LOI signer or a strategic; otherwise the index stays closed. The $34k draw cap and $5k cash floor are never breached.

watch_list.trigger: Final FAR rule in FAR Case 2023-008 (§5949) drops reliance on supplier self-certification, or a module maker pays cash because its supplier refuses a die-source declaration

Both needed (04_DEEPDIVES/private-moe-appliance.md §14.4): (a) a VAR/MSP commits in writing to >=6 boxes/yr on its own paper at <=15%/20%; and (b) a published or socket-pinned single-socket run showing >=10 tok/s per user at 4 concurrent users on a 1T-class MoE in a box quoting <=$65k (or the alternative proof listed there)
A written OCM offer of authorized-aftermarket rights (wafers, test programs, marking) for a named EOL DRAM family
Unsolicited reseller sell-through or commitment showing >=33 MRAM backup cards/month
A hi-rel cofounder arrives with an existing x72 design-in and >=3 evaluation LOIs at >=$1,200/unit

Any of Winbond, Nanya, Micron (Manassas DDR4) or a franchised distributor agrees in writing to honor a pooled multi-year allocation agreement with a no-title buying co-op (one of DD2's three $0 supplier calls)

biggest_unknown: Whether any memory-adjacent buyer will pay this part-time, non-chip founder recurring cash at all: the study contains no deposit, PO or paid pilot, and every red-team round cut demand inputs that were estimates.
monday_action: Monday 2026-11-02, <=2 hours, $0: (1) copy DD2's K0-K6 pass/fail thresholds from 04_DEEPDIVES/lifecycle-intel.md §10 into a dated doc and email it to an outside advisor to lock them; (2) read the employment agreement for IP-assignment, moonlighting, non-compete/non-solicit and confidentiality clauses and send HR a written carve-out request; (3) send DD5's $0 no-release questions to UCSC VLSIDA and Open Circuit Design.
reaim: Re-aim the project from 'make memory in America' to 'sell software to the people who buy memory', run as a capped experiment while keeping the day job. The physical U.S. memory build-out is Micron's T4, CHIPS-funded program; the openings for a <$50k founder sit beside it (procurement, lifecycle and price intelligence), not inside it.
